- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — adjust forecast downward by 2–5% to avoid overshoot.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+10% from prior 5-day avg), model often overreacts with continued upward bias — reduce forecast slope for next 3–5 days.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 30-day moving avg), model often fails to recognize — increase downward bias in forecast for next 5 days.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (e.g., -0.3 to 0.3), model tends to overestimate volatility — cap forecast range within ±3% of recent 7-day avg.
- If true outcome drops sharply after a high (e.g., >+15% spike followed by >-10% drop), model often fails to anticipate — add 1–2 day lagged correction in forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, if model consistently overpredicts by >5% in 3+ consecutive examples, apply downward bias of 5–8% to next forecast.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative sentiment), model often underestimates downside risk — add 2–4% downward buffer to forecast.
